groups.text: It is currently 21 degrees and cloudy in Berlin-Tempelhof.
With the morning weather set, here is the news.

A student has shared the results of a Bachelor's Final Project that bypasses standard software frameworks to run AI at a deeper level. The project involved implementing YOLO26n model inference from scratch using C and ARM64 Assembly Language. By extracting model parameters and redesigning the memory layout into a custom binary format, the developer aimed to understand how modern neural network inference engines function at a low level. The implementation utilized ARM NEON SIMD optimization, Winograd convolution, and cache-aware tiling to improve edge AI execution on a Raspberry Pi 4. While the system produces correct object detection results, the creator notes that performance improvements were lower than initially expected. He is now seeking feedback from the research community regarding memory layout, vectorization, and low-level neural network acceleration to further optimize the pipeline.

In Berlin, police have launched a manhunt for a twenty-one-year-old suspect named Abdul B. after a van rammed into a Pride parade near the Brandenburg Gate on Saturday night. One person was killed and sixteen others were injured, with several remaining in life-threatening condition. Authorities say Abdul B. has links to the Islamist scene and was released from juvenile detention in May. While police commandos stormed a property in the Schöneberg district overnight, they made no arrests, and the search has now extended to Germany's borders. In India, Dharmendra Pradhan has resigned as education minister following nationwide youth protests over alleged irregularities in major exams. The demonstrations were organized by the social media-driven Cockroach Janta Party, which demanded reforms and compensation for students. While Home Minister Amit Shah spoke in defense of Pradhan, the government ultimately accepted the group's demands to end the unrest.

A peaceful celebration of love and tolerance ended in tragedy in Berlin during the Christopher Street Day event. Just after 10 p.m., a white van drove into a crowd in the Tiergarten park near the Brandenburg Gate before crashing into a tree. One woman was killed, and sixteen others were injured, with three of those injuries described as life-threatening. Police spokesperson Florian Nath says they are searching for the driver, who fled the scene on foot. Meanwhile, in Tunis, nearly 2,500 people marched Saturday to protest against President Kaïs Saïed five years after his power grab. Demonstrators denounced a decline in civil liberties and deteriorating living conditions, specifically citing rising prices and scheduled power outages during a heatwave. Protesters carried signs demanding the release of prisoners and questioning where the country's development and freedom have gone while hospitals face risks from the electricity cuts.

Millions of people in Germany remain disconnected from the internet as the world becomes increasingly digital. According to the Federal Statistical Office, roughly three percent of people between 16 and 74 years old have never used the internet. This gap is most visible among older populations; while data for those over 75 is unavailable from the official office, other studies suggest that people over 80 are even less likely to be active online. Among adults aged 45 to 64, three percent report no online experience, compared to one percent of those between 25 and 44. Media scientist Moritz Büchi notes a distinction between technical access and actual participation, arguing that someone who only checks emails occasionally still counts as an onliner in statistics. This creates a divide between the two million people who have never used the web and those who simply lack meaningful digital integration.

Security forces in Balochistan have killed 16 terrorists during Operation Al-Azm, according to state media reports from Sunday. The intelligence-based operations targeted groups the government calls Fitna-al-Hindustan to highlight India's alleged role in destabilizing Pakistan. This military response follows a shooting on a coach bound for Karachi that left three people dead and five others injured. These actions come as Balochistan faces persistent security challenges, including a July 6 attack at the Mangi Dam pumping station where armed attackers killed 27 police officers. In unrelated news from the sports world, Liverpool began their tenure under manager Andoni Iraola with a 4-2 victory over Sunderland during a tour of the United States. Despite the win, the match was marred by an early injury to captain and center-back Joe Gomez, who had to be taken off in the eighth minute.

A manhunt is underway in Berlin after a driver plowed into a crowd during the city's Pride event, killing one person and wounding 16 others. Authorities warn that the suspect may be armed and dangerous. Meanwhile, in Spain, firefighters are struggling to contain spreading wildfires near Madrid and Toledo following a difficult night of combatting the blazes. Record temperatures have accelerated the spread of the fires, forcing 70,000 people to evacuate the Madrid region. Shifting to the Middle East, another night has passed without US air strikes on Iran after nearly two weeks of nightly bombardments. This pause in fighting comes as a war nears its fifth month and expands beyond the strategic Strait of Hormuz to include attacks on regional shipping and US bases. US media reports suggest the lull may be due to dwindling stockpiles of Patriot interceptors and other air defense munitions.

Security remains fragile in Niger three years after a military junta seized power in July 2023. Military leader Abdourahamane has firmly cemented his control over the country, but the social and economic improvements promised during the coup have not materialized. The situation is particularly dire in the southwestern Tillabéry region, where jihadist attacks on civilians and security forces have become more frequent and violent than they were three years ago. This escalation of violence has forced thousands of people to flee their villages, triggering a severe humanitarian crisis. In towns like Téra, residents report that schools have closed and weekly markets no longer function normally. While the military government initially suggested a transition period of no more than three years, the junta continues to hold all power as fear and instability define daily life for the population.
After the headlines, back to the weather.
This afternoon will be cloudy with temperatures between 18 and 26 degrees.
And from the weather, a quick look at the calendar.
On your calendar today: Your personal calendar has an all-day event for the twenty-twenty-six summer holidays in Berlin.
And that's it for your personal morning broadcast.
[mature adult voice, intensely emotional, tender, radiant; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
[very very long pause before speaking; then mature adult voice, most emotional, strong, warm, radiant, deeply encouraging; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
